questions.question: Which best describes the role of cuBLAS in LLM inference pipelines?
questions.choice_A: A distributed serving framework that routes requests across clusters
questions.choice_B: A GPU-optimized linear algebra library providing high-performance GEMM primitives used by transformer kernels
questions.choice_C: A CPU-only library for vectorized quantization and dequantization
questions.choice_D: A quantization toolkit for calibrating models to INT8

questions.question: What is a primary advantage of using NVIDIA FasterTransformer for serving large language models?
questions.choice_A: It replaces attention with recurrent networks to reduce compute
questions.choice_B: It compiles models to FPGAs for ultra-low latency
questions.choice_C: It provides fused, hand-optimized transformer kernels (e.g., attention, layer norm) that exploit tensor cores and mixed precision for higher throughput
questions.choice_D: It only targets CPUs to minimize GPU memory usage

questions.question: What is oneDNN primarily designed for in the context of LLM inference?
questions.choice_A: Cross-device scheduling and request batching across GPUs
questions.choice_B: Memory-mapped KV cache paging on GPUs
questions.choice_C: Training-time distributed data parallel synchronization
questions.choice_D: High-performance, vectorized primitives on CPUs (e.g., AVX-512) to accelerate inference on Intel-class hardware

questions.question: Which statement about INT8 quantization for LLM inference is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: It reduces memory bandwidth and improves throughput, but may require calibration to control accuracy loss
questions.choice_B: It always increases accuracy because of better integer rounding
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for GEMM kernels entirely
questions.choice_D: It is incompatible with transformer attention layers

questions.question: What is a typical characteristic of 2-bit quantized kernels in LLM inference?
questions.choice_A: They are universally faster than FP16 across all batch sizes
questions.choice_B: They yield extreme memory compression but require efficient dequantization and careful scaling to avoid large accuracy drops
questions.choice_C: They cannot be implemented on GPUs due to bit-packing
questions.choice_D: They remove the need for KV caches at decode time

questions.question: What are “ladder-style” kernels intended to optimize in quantized inference?
questions.choice_A: Model sharding across heterogeneous nodes
questions.choice_B: Gradient synchronization among data-parallel replicas
questions.choice_C: Tokenizer throughput during preprocessing
questions.choice_D: Dequantization and accumulation steps through staged, branch-minimized code paths that map well to SIMD/SIMT execution

questions.question: What is a key innovation in vLLM that enables high throughput under heavy concurrency?
questions.choice_A: Replacing softmax with max pooling
questions.choice_B: Training-time low-rank adapters
questions.choice_C: PagedAttention, which virtualizes the KV cache to reduce fragmentation and enable efficient memory sharing across requests
questions.choice_D: Compilation to custom ASICs

questions.question: Which capability is commonly provided by NVIDIA Triton Inference Server for serving LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Dynamic batching and multi-framework model hosting with configurable scheduling policies
questions.choice_B: On-device training to update model weights in real time
questions.choice_C: Automatic quantization to 2-bit without calibration
questions.choice_D: Replacing CUDA kernels with Python loops for debuggability

questions.question: Why is llama.cpp frequently used for edge or resource-constrained deployments?
questions.choice_A: It relies exclusively on cloud TPUs for inference
questions.choice_B: It uses lightweight C/C++ backends with aggressive quantization (e.g., 4-bit) and minimal dependencies to run on CPUs and small GPUs
questions.choice_C: It requires multi-node clusters to start
questions.choice_D: It only supports FP32 for maximum accuracy

questions.question: Which consideration is most important when deploying LLMs at the edge?
questions.choice_A: Maximizing context length regardless of memory
questions.choice_B: Preferring FP32 to avoid any quantization artifacts
questions.choice_C: Disabling batching to minimize complexity
questions.choice_D: Balancing model size and quantization level with limited compute/memory, while meeting latency and privacy constraints

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes data, model (tensor), and pipeline parallelism?
questions.choice_A: Data parallelism partitions layers across devices; model parallelism replicates the model; pipeline parallelism shards weights within layers
questions.choice_B: All three strategies use the same communication pattern (all-reduce) each step
questions.choice_C: Data parallelism replicates weights across devices and splits batches; model (tensor) parallelism shards individual layers across devices; pipeline parallelism splits layers into stages executed in a pipeline
questions.choice_D: Pipeline parallelism requires no inter-device communication

questions.question: What does GPipe specifically refer to in the context of pipeline parallelism?
questions.choice_A: A micro-batch scheduling method that splits the model into stages and overlaps forward/backward passes to reduce pipeline bubbles
questions.choice_B: A quantization scheme for gating experts in MoE models
questions.choice_C: A CPU kernel library for attention
questions.choice_D: A tokenizer optimized for GPU execution

questions.question: Which benchmarking statement is most accurate for LLM serving?
questions.choice_A: Throughput is best measured as queries per second only
questions.choice_B: Latency should only be measured as average; percentiles add no value
questions.choice_C: Warmup runs should be excluded because they mimic steady state
questions.choice_D: Both latency percentiles (e.g., p50, p95) and throughput (e.g., tokens/sec), measured under realistic load and batching, are necessary for meaningful comparisons

questions.question: During autoregressive decoding, what often dominates memory usage and affects batching capacity?
questions.choice_A: Optimizer states
questions.choice_B: The key-value (KV) cache size, which grows with sequence length and batch size
questions.choice_C: Embedding table reads during tokenization
questions.choice_D: Activation checkpoints used only in training

questions.question: Which practice helps ensure a fair, apples-to-apples performance comparison across inference libraries?
questions.choice_A: Using the same model, precision, sequence lengths, batch sizes, and enabling proper warmup before measuring
questions.choice_B: Comparing FP16 to INT8 because they are commonly used
questions.choice_C: Measuring only single-token latency with empty prompts
questions.choice_D: Disabling logging and telemetry to reduce overhead

questions.question: What is a common trade-off of dynamic batching in serving frameworks like Triton?
questions.choice_A: It decreases throughput but improves latency
questions.choice_B: It eliminates the need for GPU memory
questions.choice_C: It increases throughput by forming larger batches but can increase per-request latency due to waiting for batch formation
questions.choice_D: It prevents multi-model hosting on a single server

questions.question: How does quantization-aware training (QAT) differ from post-training quantization (PTQ) for LLM inference?
questions.choice_A: QAT is done after deployment; PTQ happens during training
questions.choice_B: QAT simulates quantization during training to recover accuracy under low bit-widths, while PTQ calibrates an already trained model without weight updates
questions.choice_C: PTQ requires labeled data; QAT does not
questions.choice_D: They are identical in methodology and outcomes

questions.question: When choosing between cuBLAS and oneDNN for deployment, which statement is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: cuBLAS is preferred on CPUs; oneDNN is preferred on GPUs
questions.choice_B: Both target only ARM CPUs
questions.choice_C: oneDNN is mandatory for tensor parallelism
questions.choice_D: cuBLAS typically targets NVIDIA GPUs, while oneDNN targets CPUs (particularly Intel), so the hardware stack largely determines the choice

questions.question: Which capability helps manage complex production deployments with multiple LLMs and versions?
questions.choice_A: PagedAttention in vLLM
questions.choice_B: Ladder-style dequant kernels
questions.choice_C: A serving platform like Triton that supports model repositories, versioning, ensembles, and per-model scheduling
questions.choice_D: A CPU-only runtime like llama.cpp

questions.question: Which statement about communication overheads in parallel LLM inference is correct?
questions.choice_A: Data parallelism introduces zero overhead because weights are replicated
questions.choice_B: Tensor (model) parallelism often requires frequent collectives (e.g., all-reduce) within layers, while pipeline parallelism introduces pipeline bubbles; data parallelism scales more easily but replicates weights across devices
questions.choice_C: Pipeline parallelism removes the need for KV caches
questions.choice_D: All parallel strategies have identical scaling behavior
